title: "My Experience at BIO 25"
description: "Reflections from attending the largest biotech event in Boston."
date: 2025-08-01
categories: [conference, biotech]
---

I was fortunate to be selected as one of the student scholars at BIO 25, the largest and most comprehensive biotechnology event held this year in Boston.

Attending the conference was an enriching experience — I had the chance to explore the vast landscape of biotechnology, connect with ambitious peers, and hear directly from leaders driving innovation in the field.

Highlights

🌟 Student networking events These sessions were a great opportunity to meet fellow students who were passionate, ambitious, and eager to make an impact. Being in such a dynamic environment was motivating and inspiring.

🌟 Exhibit hall The exhibit booths were another highlight. I connected with biotech representatives from across the U.S. and around the world. The Mexico pavilion stood out in particular, featuring a live mariachi band and dance performance that drew a big crowd.

🌟 City of South San Francisco event I also attended a networking event hosted by the City of South San Francisco, where I learned about the city’s deep connection to the biotech industry and met several industry leaders in an engaging setting.

Key Takeaways

Investment climate: Venture capitalists are cautious given economic uncertainty and questions about the sustainability of the AI boom. Still, as one attendee noted, these cycles are temporary, and upward trends often follow.

Emerging areas: Neuroinflammation and "digital twins" ([Baptista, 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/d43747-022-00108-3)) are gaining attention as promising, underexplored fields.

Longevity & tech: Longevity research continues to grow, with major tech companies like NVIDIA expanding their presence in healthcare.

Final Thoughts

BIO 25 was a fantastic opportunity to gain insights into life sciences innovation, discover new areas of research, and build connections with people across the biotech ecosystem. I came away inspired and more aware of the diverse directions the field is heading.
